pairs.subject: voice-io
pairs.evidence: src/athena/channels/voice/gateway.py:535 When a push-to-talk hold crosses the 2-minute MAX_UTTERANCE_BYTES cap, the gateway throws away the whole utterance and tells the person to release the key sooner; stt-pipeline says the cap closes a segment, transcribes it and keeps capturing, so up to two minutes of speech is lost instead of segmented.

techniques.evidence: src/athena/channels/voice/gateway.py:535 At the cap the whole utterance is dropped, not segmented. Everything else is honest: the level gate (backends.py:366) and typed too_short/silent/no_words outcomes with peak_dbfs on the final transcript (gateway.py:934). That refutes the stale 'silent collapse' finding.

src/athena/channels/voice/config.py:187 If the stored config names a retired voice, model or engine, the whole choice (STT pick included) silently resets to defaults with no record or note. The technique wants the one door to map to a successor and record that it did. Probes do give absent/broken/ready.

src/athena/channels/voice/kokoro.py:10 Kokoro starts a new sherpa-onnx process per sentence and reloads the model every time, which is the named failure. Rendering the next sentence early hides the gap between sentences, but every reply's first audio still pays the cold load, and there is no resident mode and no both-ways measurement.

src/athena/channels/voice/backends.py:89 The engine layer raises one untyped error for not-installed, timeout and engine failure, so no host route can map the four answers. The shared per-user home with Personas (home.py:6) is conformant.
src/athena/channels/voice/tts.py:44 Both the TTS line and the visible-text fallback pass the speech.speakable door, which owns the sentence-boundary rules. Refutes the stale tts.py:41 finding.

src/athena/channels/voice/gateway.py:798 Each line takes a generation id at enqueue time. A barge-in raises the cutoff, so the playing line stops at its next chunk and the generator is closed; error, barge_in and done are distinct stop reasons.

src/athena/channels/voice/commands.py:149 One parser per channel; the grammar is the cards on screen right now; matching is exact or by synonym, never fuzzy. Unmatched speech becomes a message to the model rather than being dropped.
src/athena/channels/voice/config.py:114 Local hearing is the default. compose() never falls back to the cloud: if the chosen listener is not ready, voice is off with a reason. The key is sealed.
src/athena/channels/voice/whisper.py:176 The adapter drops whisper's [BLANK_AUDIO]-style markers, a level gate runs before the engine, and no prompt biasing is used.
src/athena/channels/voice/gateway.py:946 The transcript goes to a reasoning model, so no cleanup stage runs. That matches the technique's 'destination is a model' exclusion.
src/athena/channels/voice/kokoro.py:580 The host's silence scaling is replayed as a time map for the visemes; face events are stamped with the line's generation.
src/athena/channels/voice/install.py:95 Rule 7: one per-user engine home shared with Personas, plus an exclusive install lock. Pinned SHA-256 and size, and a visible install state machine.
src/athena/channels/voice/backends.py:143 No vendor-owned conversation; the provider is only used for STT/TTS.
src/athena/channels/voice/kokoro.py:23 The catalog is one voice; no described or cloned voices.
src/athena/channels/voice/gateway.py:1013 Speech is only said in reply to a turn started on the socket itself; there is no second door for unhosted callers.
src/athena/channels/voice/gateway.py:1081 The only other say() caller is the same socket's card answer. One persona voice by design, no automated callers.
src/athena/channels/voice/config.py:86 Kokoro fixes durations before rendering, the technique's own measured exclusion, and a person is present. This rests on Kokoro's engine class, not on code here.
src/athena/channels/voice/gateway.py:803 The daemon streams frames over the socket; it opens no device and nothing waits for playback to end.
src/athena/channels/voice/commands.py:11 Transcripts go into the product's own lane, never to a foreign cursor or the clipboard.

pairs.registryProposal: stt-pipeline's cap rule could name the middle option seen here: refuse the utterance and say so the moment the cap is hit. It is honest, but it still loses the capture; say whether that is ever acceptable for push-to-talk.

techniques.evidence: src/athena/daemon/voice.py:100 Unavailable, timeout and engine failure collapse into one status and code; no throttle on the routes. Served-engine headers are present (X-Tts-Provider at :107).

pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/src/modules/setup/index.ts:53 The microphone answer is hook-local state seeded 'unknown', so a denial is forgotten on the next visit (micFact reads 'not asked yet'). The denied arm carries only the raw webview message, so someone who refused once is never told how to re-grant push-to-talk.

techniques.evidence: apps/desktop/src/modules/setup/readiness.ts:154 Denial is distinct from no-device (NotFoundError maps to unsupported), but it is not remembered and has no platform re-grant instructions.
apps/desktop/src/modules/setup/readiness.ts:181 Neither mic nor voice is required for readiness: voice stays an overlay channel.
apps/desktop/src/modules/setup/readiness.ts:170 The voice fact is phrased from the daemon's live readiness reason, not from a remembered flag.

pairs.registryProposal: stt-pipeline's 'denial is remembered' could say where the memory belongs in a webview: read the platform's own permission state (a permissions query) rather than keep a product-side copy that can disagree with it.
